scenes.headline:
Why does this
query *fail*?
scenes.voiceover: This query looks fine. So why does it *fail?*

scenes.headline:
You write
*SELECT first*
scenes.voiceover: You write SELECT first. But SQL does *not start* there.
scenes.tts: You write SELECT first. But S Q L does not start there.

scenes.headline:
SQL starts
at *FROM*
scenes.voiceover: It starts at *FROM.* First it finds the table.

scenes.headline:
Then *WHERE*
filters the rows
scenes.voiceover: Second, *WHERE* keeps the rows it needs.

scenes.headline:
*SELECT* runs
near the end
scenes.voiceover: Only then does *SELECT* add them up and name the total.

scenes.headline:
*ORDER BY*
sorts last
scenes.voiceover: Last of all, *ORDER BY* sorts the answer.

scenes.headline:
Written order is not
the *logical order*
scenes.voiceover: So the order you write is not the order SQL *works through* it.
scenes.tts: So the order you write is not the order S Q L works through it.

scenes.headline:
It came *before*
the name existed
scenes.voiceover: The filter came before SELECT *named the total.* That is the error.

scenes.headline:
Test totals
in *HAVING*
scenes.voiceover: Move the test to *HAVING,* after the groups, and it works.

scenes.headline:
Read a query in
its *logical order*
scenes.voiceover: Read a query in *that order* and errors make sense.
Follow *DataEntropy* for more SQL explained simply.
scenes.tts: Follow Data Entropy for more S Q L explained simply.
